examples.description: The newest 20 invoices with balances and state
The overdue invoices to chase, 50 at a time

failure_modes.recovery: Resend with one of the listed states, or without state to list every invoice.
failure_modes.when: state is not one of draft, sent, partially_paid, overdue, written_off, paid, cancelled

preconditions: Totals and state are never stored columns: every row is enriched on read with total_cents, remaining_cents, state and is_overdue. GET /api/sales/overview adds aging and per-currency stats.

description: Lists your invoices, newest first (200 at most; pass limit and cursor to page). Every row carries the same worked-out money and state as invoice_read: total_cents, remaining_cents, state, is_overdue, days_overdue (integer CENTS, business days). To find what to chase, pass state 'overdue': only invoices issued, still owed and due before today in the business time zone come back. payer_confirmations_pending counts the payer's "I've paid" reports waiting on each row. Refuses an unlisted state, a limit outside 1-200 or a malformed cursor with VALIDATION_ERROR: resend with a listed state, without limit, or with next_cursor exactly as returned.

cursor.description: Opaque page cursor — pass a previous response's next_cursor verbatim. null next_cursor means no further pages.

limit.description: Page size 1-200. Omit BOTH limit and cursor for the legacy bare-array first page of 200; pass either to get { items, next_cursor, limit } instead.

state.description: Only invoices in this worked-out state, still newest first and paged the same way. Leave it out for every invoice.

name: invoice_list
